### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/driver-mongodb`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/README.md`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object datasourceDriverMongoToMongodb), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object datasourceDriverMongoToMongodb))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/README.md`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `98d738bd7237c0012dd50e49e81a249fe93be730` — the merge of head `acf0e6c1faddeadab933358e5bedaa3fae075f2f` into base `16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 98d738bd7237c0012dd50e49e81a249fe93be730 && git checkout 98d738bd7237c0012dd50e49e81a249fe93be730
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17 acf0e6c1faddeadab933358e5bedaa3fae075f2f && git checkout -B drift-repro 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17 && git merge --no-ff acf0e6c1faddeadab933358e5bedaa3fae075f2f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · session `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk` · 2026-10-15T04:32Z

This is the seat review of record for #23543 family F1 (claim `6182201116`, ruling `6182001882`) on head:

`acf0e6c1faddeadab933358e5bedaa3fae075f2f`

It is not the contract review. That review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` because `packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts` and the registry are published schema.

1. **Form.**

   - No `content/docs/releases/` change.
   - 23 files, +557/−162.
   - Not governed: `check-governed-merges --pr 23600` hits 0 of 23 paths.
2. **Premises measured.** Before this change, a `driver: 'mongo'` passed `defineStack` silently (the dev's dist probe). PM mechanism assumption 1 is partly falsified, and the dev's route stands:

   - So the spelling leaves authoring (`DriverType` refuses it by name) and boot selection, and stays only on the contract face (`resolveDriverId('mongo')` still answers `mongodb`) for stored rows.
   - Whether that remnant is a "double spelling" against ruling item 7 is the contract review's ③ to judge.
3. **Gates.**
   - Check-runs on this head: 41 in all, 36 success, 5 skipped, none red or pending. That includes Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, and Test Core 1–6.
   - Locally the dev ran 112 of the 117 derived families. The other 5 are NOT MEASURED, each with a reason.
   - `check:platform-checklist`'s red is on `main`'s tree, outside this diff.
4. **Accepted deviations.**
   - The refusal is a regex `pattern` on the open `z.string()`, derived from a new `retiredAliases` column. That spelling survives the JSON Schema projection.
   - One new public export, `RETIRED_DRIVER_ID_GUIDANCE`.
   - The pin-sweep and false-text files beyond the claim's list are named in the report, and `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` is untouched.
   - Declared narrowing: `runtime`'s `test:repo` is left to CI per the seat's lock note.
   - This record amends the claim's surface to the PR's file list.
5. **Out-of-scope findings.**
   - (1) `check:platform-checklist` red on `main`: dropped. The daily watchdog files and owns that card (today's instance is #23593).
   - (2) The re-pointed `os migrate meta --from 16` suites lose their last real subject once F3 and F2 land. The carrier is the F3 and F2 dispatches on #23543, from this seat. Their dispatch orders will name it.
6. **Prose checked against the diff.**
   - `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`: the two table rows drop `mongo`. The new paragraph says "an authored `driver: 'mongo'` is refused with the prescription naming `mongodb`" (`DriverType`'s guidance regex) and "stored datasource rows keep loading" (the rehydration seams replay the retired conversion, per `DriverType`'s docblock).
   - The five secret-key rows now read `mongodb` only.
   - `packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/README.md`: "recognised value: `mongodb`; the old `mongo` spelling was retired in `@objectstack/spec` 18 and is refused".
   - The changeset: BREAKING, with the migration list and the stored-row paragraph.
   - The bump levels (`spec` minor, `driver-mongodb` patch) are the contract review's ②.
7. **The dev's open question** (should the PR body line carry the arm?): **B, it stays `Clause-②: yes`.** The claim line's machine spelling is exactly `yes` or `no`. The `(narrowing)` arm lives in the changeset, where the ADR-0087 gate read it green.
8. **Landing terms.** First a contract review PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the head, then every check green, then the seat marks the PR ready and enables auto-merge. `needs:contract-review` stays on this PR until then. On merge, #23543 is released to `pm:queue` with F5-jsx, F3, F2, F4 and F5-http left.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `acf0e6c1faddeadab933358e5bedaa3fae075f2f`
Local-runs: none

Family F1 of ruling 6182001882 on card #23543, PR #23600, read at 2026-10-15T04:49Z. Inputs: the card body and its nine comments, the PR body and its 23-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge-base `32e03d2fd` (+557/−162, equal to the three-dot diff against `origin/main`), and the 45 check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run; every tree reading below is `git show` / `git grep` against the fetched head.

**Gate verdicts on this head:** 45 check-runs, 37 `success`, 8 `skipped`, 0 failing or pending. The five required contexts — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and 1–6/6), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` — are all `success`; so are `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the four `Type Check ·` lanes, the nine `Lint ·` lanes, and the card, claim and single-writer guards. The 8 `skipped` are the PR fast-set skips (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, the dogfood shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the opt-in packed-tarball smoke, and the re-fired `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` duplicates); those families are `main`'s full battery and are NOT MEASURED on the PR by design. Correction to the dev report (6184434243): it lists `Console Pin Gate` and `Temporal Conformance` among the successes; on this head both are `skipped`.

Governance: none of the 23 paths is in `GOVERNED_SURFACES` (register read on the head); head repo equals base repo; 719 changed lines; no `content/docs/releases/` edit; `Part of #23543` is the first line and no closing keyword follows; draft; the assignee mirrors the card's.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes (each narrows what an author or operator may write):

1. **`DriverType` refuses `mongo` by name** (`packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts`): `z.string()` gains one `.regex()` per `RETIRED_DRIVER_ID_GUIDANCE` key — for `mongo`, a negative lookahead over the whitespace-trimmed, case-folded spelling, with the prescription as the message. Refused: `mongo`, `Mongo`, ` MONGO `, a tab-and-newline-wrapped `mongo`; still accepted: `mongodb`, every other builtin, `com.vendor.mongolike`, `xmongo`, `mongo.v2`, `__proto__`, `constructor`, and the empty string (as before). Reported as zod `invalid_format` at path `driver`, and the config gate still runs behind it (`driver` and `config` both reported on a misspelled key), so the refusal hides nothing. At `defineStack` it is `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 with one issue at `datasources.0.driver`. **RIGHT** — this is ruling F1 A's "refused with the prescription naming `mongodb`", at every door that parses a datasource. The open namespace stays open (a `z.string()`; `enumWithRetiredValues` cannot carry it), and the regex spelling — not a refinement — is what lets the refusal survive the JSON Schema projection as a `pattern` (pinned in `config-registry.test.ts`), so a document validated against the published `json-schema/**` is refused too. The schema's input type is still `string`; `tsc` cannot carry a value refusal on an open string, so the parse-time prescription is the whole channel here, as ruling item 7 says.
2. **Selection face narrows** (`config-registry.zod.ts`): the `mongodb` row's `aliases` drop `mongo`; `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_ALIASES` goes 14 → 13; `resolveDatabaseDriverId('mongo')` → `undefined`; `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS` unchanged. Both boot hosts read that one table (`packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts` `DatabaseDriverSelectionSchema` through `resolveDatabaseDriverId`; `packages/cli` `resolveDriverType` and `database-driver-flag.ts` through the selection faces), so `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=mongo`, `databaseDriver: 'mongo'` and `--database-driver mongo` are all refused with the hosts' "Supported drivers" list, which names `mongodb`. **RIGHT**; the cross-host parity pin (`driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts`) is flipped to assert exactly this. The dev's acceptance note holds: the host refusal is the generic list, not a dedicated prescription sentence; the list names the right spelling, and `RETIRED_DRIVER_ID_GUIDANCE` is exported for a host that wants to name it later.
3. **`datasource-driver-mongo-to-mongodb` leaves the load path** (`conversions/registry.ts`): `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`. The authoring funnel no longer rewrites an authored `mongo` (the new test asserts the stack unchanged and zero notices), so the author meets judgment 1 instead of a silent rewrite with a notice. Data at rest keeps replaying it: `applyConversionsToStoredItem` (`includeRetired` pinned true), the artifact door, and `os migrate meta --from 16` — the id is already a step-17 `conversionIds` member (`migrations/registry.ts.template:1126`), ordered after `datasource-config-driver-key-aliases`, which still reaches a stored `mongo` row's legacy keys because of judgment 5. **RIGHT.** `'17.7.0'` is the value `conversions/types.ts`'s own `retiredAfter` docblock gives for an `18.0.0-next.N` label (the package reads `18.0.0-next.1`), it matches the seven #23487 retirements, and `retired-after.census.test.ts` pins it against the published tarballs.
4. **Verdict-list pin** (`conversions.test.ts`): the entry moves from the kept list (now 7 entries, the five remaining families) to the retired list with `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`; the `describe` block now asserts the four facts that must hold together — a stored row still converges and then parses; the funnel no longer rewrites; an authored `mongo` meets the prescription at `defineStack`; an unconverted stored row keeps its contract. The removal-version pin (`retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts`) gains the entry's refusal row in its `JOIN`, so every retired entry still has a renderer. **RIGHT** — ruling item 7's "verdict-list pin updated", and the kept-without-ruling list shrinks by exactly one.
5. **Contract face kept — not an accept-set change; judged in ③ below:** `DRIVER_ID_ALIASES` still maps `mongo` → `mongodb` (now through the new `retiredAliases` column instead of `aliases`), so `resolveDriverId('mongo')`, `getDriverConfigSchema('mongo')` and `validateDriverConfig('mongo', …)` answer exactly what they answered before. Pinned both ways in `config-registry.test.ts`: a retired spelling is no row's live id or alias (so the refusal can never fire on a legal value), and every retired spelling still resolves a contract; the anti-vacuity line asserts the table carries exactly `['mongo']`.

Public-surface changes (widenings):

6. **New export `RETIRED_DRIVER_ID_GUIDANCE`** — a frozen read-only record, retired spelling → prescription (`api-surface/data.json` +1, `export-origins/data.json` +1). **RIGHT** — `DriverType` reads it cross-module through an import `datasource.zod.ts` already had, so no new cycle; this is the one widening the body's `Clause-②: yes` declares.
7. **`DriverVocabularyEntry.retiredAliases?: RetiredValueGuidance`** — an optional member added to an exported interface; additive for every reader; the `as const satisfies` row still type-checks. **RIGHT.** Reusing `RetiredValueGuidance` keeps one prescription vocabulary with `enumWithRetiredValues` instead of a second.
8. **Published JSON Schema `data/Datasource` gains `pattern` on `driver`.** `json-schema.manifest/data.json` is a names-only list (`data/Datasource`), so no manifest regeneration is owed and none is missing; the projection itself is built, not tracked, and the pattern is pinned. **RIGHT.**
9. **D3 entry `18.datasource-driver-mongo-alias-retired.ts`** — a `SemanticMigration` in the sibling shape (375 `18.*` entries beside it), `conversionIds: ['datasource-driver-mongo-to-mongodb']`, naming what the chain cannot reach (`OS_DATABASE_DRIVER`, a standalone stack's `databaseDriver`, REST writers). `gen:migration-registry` writes the gitignored registry; `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` rode green. **RIGHT** — the family's one D3 entry, which the registry docblock records the 17 rename never had.
10. **Docs and comments**: `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx` (two table rows drop `mongo`, one retirement paragraph), `packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/README.md` (published, hence the `patch` row), the `liveness/datasource.json` note, and comments in `driver-catalog.ts`, `mongo.zod.ts`, `mongo.test.ts` and `cli/src/utils/config.ts`. **RIGHT.** A head-tree sweep for residual `mongo` writers outside tests finds only these, one historical quotation already marked false (`mongo.zod.ts:26` and its generated reflection), and `datasource-credential-redaction.ts:203`, whose "a stored legacy `driver: 'mongo'` row is scrubbed identically" stays true under judgment 5. `content/docs/references/` is untouched (the `mongo.zod.ts` edit is a code comment, not a `.describe()`), and the release page the drift-check flagged read-only was correctly not edited.
11. **Four load-path suites re-pointed** (`stack-authored-input.test.ts`; cli `migrate-meta-load-conversions`, `migrate-meta-composed-load-conversions`, and the load-path case of `migrate-meta-composed`) from `driver: 'mongo'` onto a flow-level `errorHandling.retryDelayMs`, renamed by `retry-policy-converged` (live, a step-17 member). **RIGHT for F1**: these suites test the authored-input shim, which needs a spelling the load still converts, and `mongo` no longer is one. Two fixtures in `datasource.test.ts` move to `mongodb` with unchanged assertions. The cost is named in ③.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23543-f1-retire-mongo-driver-alias.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/driver-mongodb: patch`; summary `feat(spec)!:`; `**BREAKING (authoring):**` banner; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; FROM → TO for all three places the spelling lives; the `os migrate meta --from 16` sentence; the ADR-0087 disposition marker `registered datasource-driver-mongo-alias-retired`. **RIGHT.** The repo is in Changesets pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`), where a BREAKING spec change grades `minor`; the two precedents on the head, `23421-retire-page-aliases-at-18.md` and `23487-retire-overdue-conversions.md`, carry the identical frontmatter, banner and arm shape. `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it as `BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing, registered`; `Check Changeset` is `success`. The `patch` for `driver-mongodb` matches a published README text change. `cli` and `service-datasource` moved only comments and need no row; the hosts' refusal change is the spec row's and is described there.
- **The `Clause-②:` line.** The changeset's `yes (narrowing)` is the right arm: the diff widens one surface (judgment 6) and narrows others (judgments 1–3). The PR body's line reads bare `Clause-②: yes`, which `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines as "a widening" with no arm. That is true of the diff but not the whole of it, and ruling item 7 spells the arm. It is not a false declaration and no gate's verdict turns on it (`check-changeset-no-major` reads the body's `yes` and finds `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`; the breaking-signal reader takes the arm from the changeset), so it does not fail this record — but the body line is the PR-scoped carrier and should read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` before the PR is armed. See ③ item 1.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions` (6184434243):

1. *Should the PR body's `Clause-②: yes` gain the arm?* **Answered: A.** The owning seat amends the body line to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — one line, the body read back after the write, no second footer (AGENTS.md's PR-body rule). Where the gap came from: the claim comment 6182201116 itself wrote `Clause-②: yes`, and the dev copied it as instructed, so the dispatch's line is what is short, not the dev's copy. Not a verdict condition, for the reasons in ②.

Dev `deviations`:

2. *Mechanism assumption 1 changed route — the alias left selection and authoring but kept the contract face, instead of being deleted.* **Accepted as the right call, and the seat review's open question — is the remnant a "double spelling" under ruling item 7 — is answered NO.** Item 7's "no staged window and no double spelling" governs what the doors accept from an author or operator; after this PR nothing an author or operator writes is accepted as `mongo`: the parse refuses it, both hosts refuse it, the published JSON Schema refuses it. What remains is the data-at-rest resolver, the same posture the retired in-memory engine's spellings already hold (`contractOnlyAliases`), and it is load-bearing: `datasource-credential-redaction.ts` keys its mongodb passthrough-secret table by canonical id through `resolveDriverId` (`:231`, `:245`, `:378`), and `datasource-credential-redaction.test.ts:341` and `:481` pin a stored legacy `mongo` row's scrub. The dev's measurement — with the alias deleted, a raw stored legacy row served all ten mongodb passthrough secrets in cleartext — is the failure those pins exist to catch. Ruling F1's "stored rows are rewritten once by the D3 chain" describes the row after the chain reaches it; the kept face protects the raw read path before then, and ADR-0087's addendum already has every data-at-rest seam replaying retired entries. The guard against this face ever becoming a second accepted spelling is pinned: a `retiredAliases` key may be no row's id or alias.
3. *The refusal is a regex `pattern`, not `enumWithRetiredValues`; a first `superRefine` was refused by the dropped-refinement gate.* **Accepted** — `driver` is an open `z.string()`; a refinement would not project; `pattern` does and is pinned; the prescription type and its writing conventions are the helper's.
4. *New public export `RETIRED_DRIVER_ID_GUIDANCE`.* **Accepted** (judgment 6); declared in the changeset and by the body's `yes`.
5. *Files outside the claim's literal list.* **Accepted** — each is a pin-sweep or false-text hit named in the report; the diff's only `registry.ts` hunk is the `datasource-driver-mongo-to-mongodb` docblock and its two new fields; `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` and every other entry are untouched, as the claim required.
6. *Declared narrowing: `runtime` `test:repo` left to CI after the PM's lock note.* **Accepted** — `Test Core` 1–6 and the aggregate are `success` on this head.
7. *A locked closure build killed by `timeout 590` and re-run clean; the harness's model-named trailer not used.* **Accepted** — process notes; `check:commit-card-trailers` rode green on every push.

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`:

8. *`check:platform-checklist` red on `origin/main`'s tree, zero overlap with this diff.* Kept out of per-PR CI by decision; the seat review names the watchdog's card (#23593) as the owner. **Not this PR's.**
9. *After this PR the load-path conversions `os migrate meta --from 16` replays are `retry-policy-converged` and F3's two lifts; the four re-pointed suites lose their last real subject when F2 and F3 land.* **Escalated to the F3 and F2 dispatch orders on #23543, as the seat review already carried it:** whichever of those PRs lands last must give the authored-input shim a synthetic probe or retire the suites. The fixtures state `maxRetries: 3`, so F2's loud form does not touch them; it is the retirement of the `retryDelayMs` rename that removes their subject.

Report corrections, not flags: the dev report counts 41 check-runs with `Console Pin Gate` and `Temporal Conformance` among the successes; on this head there are 45 (re-fired label and size runs), and those two are `skipped` on the PR, measured by `main`'s full battery. No gate verdict changes.

Premise re-read on the head: no `examples/**` or `packages/apps/**` source authors `driver: 'mongo'`; the Setup catalog's `id` is `mongodb`. F1 names no objectui follow-up and this PR owes none.
